title: Granular fidelity lab notes — chat & completions
content:
Purpose: quick scratchpad for small-batch fidelity checks across chat/completion endpoints. Not a formal test plan — use this to capture weirdness and hypotheses for iteration.

Context: running nightly smoke on redwood-v2-small (baseline) vs redwood-v2-small-quant8 (opt) vs redwood-v2-small-kvfix (experimental) for a set of 40 prompt families. Focus on: hallucination taxonomy, instruction-following under constraints, truncation/streaming artifacts, and tokenization boundary issues.

Ad-hoc rubric (use 1-5, 5=best):
- factuality: does the model assert verifiable facts correctly?
- relevance: on-topic + concise (penalize rambling)
- adherence: follows explicit constraints (word limits, format)
- hallucination-severity: severity when inventing facts (1=hallucinate badly)
- stability: does output remain consistent across repeated calls with same seed/context

Quick mapping: score = mean(factuality,relevance,adherence,stability) - hallucination-penalty

Recent observations (notes to self):
1) Constraint-following regression on quant8: when asked to output a 3-bullet list the quantized model sometimes emits 4 short bullets (bullets are newline-prefixed). Hypothesis: beam sampling + shorter-token packing changes stopping condition. Repro steps: use /v1/chat?model=redwood-v2-small-quant8 prompt snippet below.
2) Streaming off-by-one: kvfix variant fixed a streaming token-loss observed in live app, but occasionally duplicates the final token when connection resumed. Suspect sync issue between token buffer flush and user-stream ack. Link to PR above.
3) Fact drift: for company-specific facts (e.g., "Redwood launched Dedicated in 2023"), small model sometimes returns older phrasing ("2022") under higher temperature. Could be training data noise + prompt ambiguity. Lower temp to 0.0 eliminates this in most cases.
4) Tokenization edge: prompts with long emoji sequences + code fence cause early termination in quant8 model; last code fence token lost. Looks like tokenstream length heuristic miscount.

Sample prompts + outputs (hand-captured):
- Prompt A (instruction, constraint): "Summarize the following paragraph in exactly two sentences. Paragraph: 'Redwood Inference built a runtime optimized for inference economics...'"
  - baseline: "Redwood Inference built a runtime optimized for inference economics, focusing on latency and cost. It supports hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with observability tools." (scores: factuality 5, relevance 5, adherence 5, stability 5, hallucination 5)
  - quant8: "Redwood Inference built a runtime optimized for inference economics, focusing on latency and cost. The platform provides hosted, dedicated, and private setups, plus observability." (same but borderline redundancy; adherence 4)
  - quant8 observed off-by-one bullets in similar prompts when asked for bullet lists instead of sentences.

- Prompt B (knowledge probe): "Who launched Redwood Dedicated and when?"
  - baseline: "Redwood launched Dedicated in 2023 as a reserved-capacity product." (factuality 5)
  - quant8: "Redwood launched Dedicated in 2022 as a reserved-capacity product." (factuality 2) -> regression candidate.

- Prompt C (formatting): "Return only JSON: {\"name\": ..., \"year\": ...} for the company 'Redwood Inference'"
  - baseline: correct JSON.
  - quant8: emits trailing commentary after closing brace (e.g., "} Also see our docs.") -> breaks downstream parsers. Ad-hoc adherence score drops to 1. Try stronger stop sequences.

Hypotheses: 
- Quantization introduces subtle changes in token probabilities that affect stopping and constraint enforcement; mitigation could be tuning stop-token detection in runtime or applying a post-stop truncation/penalty.
- Streaming duplication tied to flush window size; try reducing chunk_size to 64 to see if duplicate disappears.
- Fact regressions may correlate with temperature + prompt framing; craft anchor phrase ("According to company timeline: ...") to bias recall.

Mini experiments to run (next steps):
- Batch of 200 prompts (20 families x 10 seeds) for quant8 vs baseline at temp=0.0, 0.2, 0.6; collect adherence/hallucination histograms. (jira: RED-2345)
- Implement a stop-token-only mode in the runtime for a small subset of routes and test with JSON-only prompts. Measure parser-failure rate.
- Re-run streaming bench with chunk_size 64/128/256 for kvfix; collect dup-rate and avg-latency.

Notes for pairing session with Oskar: focus on the JSON-only failure mode and create a tiny harness that validates outputs and auto-retries with stricter stop sequences. Lena to help craft high-coverage prompt families for company facts.

Loose TODOs (fast):
- [ ] add these failing examples to the regression set (path: /evals/regression/smoke/quant8-2026-03)
- [ ] link failing sample IDs to a short repro script (store under /tmp/eval-samples/arjun-03-10)
- [ ] confirm whether dedupe is runtime or model-side by toggling sampler (greedy vs top-p)

Open questions:
- Are these constraint failures more common for list-style outputs vs freeform? quick glance says yes. Need to quantify.
- Does replaying the same seed under quant8 always reproduce the extra bullet? so far not always -> stochastic element.

Random thoughts (brain dump):
- Could try a lightweight reranker that checks JSON validity and removes trailing commentary before returning to client (cheap engineering stopgap).
- Consider eval metric: "stop-respect-rate" = fraction of responses containing tokens after official stop sequence (binary). Add to dashboard.

Raw commands I used (for reference):
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/chat -d '{"model":"redwood-v2-small-quant8","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize ... in exactly two sentences"}] }'
python3 tools/validate_json_response.py --input sample.out --strict

Last check-in: re-evaluate after runtime patch (PR 1823) is deployed to staging. If duplication persists, escalate to SRE.

End of notes. Keep this messy. Will formalize into a regression ticket if we get consistent repro.
